In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). If the symptoms are less severe, contact a poison control center without delay. Residents in the United States can reach the poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. 3. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next scheduled dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to make up for the missed one. 4. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed, following local disposal regulations. 5. This document is not a substitute for professional medical advice. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information tailored to your health needs. 6. Crofelemer is used to alleviate diarrhea symptoms in patients with HIV/AIDS who are undergoing treatment with antiretroviral medications. This drug may help reduce the frequency of watery stools and improve tolerance to HIV medications. Swallow the tablets whole without crushing or chewing them. Take this medication consistently to achieve the best results. It may take several months to experience the full benefits of this treatment. 7. Common side effects of this medication may include nasal congestion, runny nose, cough, sore throat, or sneezing. Remember that your doctor has prescribed this medication because they believe the benefits outweigh the potential risks. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. However, this is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for similar concerns. 8. Before starting crofelemer, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used if clearly necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk, so consult your doctor before breastfeeding. 9. Drug interactions may alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not cover all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal supplements, and share this list with your doctor and pharmacist. 10. If someone has overdosed and is experiencing severe symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. For less severe cases, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222 for assistance. 11. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not take extra medication to compensate for the missed dose. 12. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Dispose of this product properly when it is expired or no longer needed, following local waste disposal guidelines.
